blocks.text: Delirium

Delirium or acute confusion state is a condition characterized by disturbance in attention accompanied with reduced awareness of the environment; develops over a short period of time and fluctuates in severity.

Non-Pharmacological Management
Control the acute disturbance.
Patients who actively walk with symptoms of agitation or restlessness require close observation within a safe and reasonably closed environment.

Schizophrenia
It is a chronic mental disorder, characterized by disturbances in thought, emotions, drive, behavior and withdrawal from reality.
Clinical Presentation
Symptoms vary from patient to patient and from time to time. To diagnose Schizophrenia, the following criteria need to be met;
Presence of 2 or more of the following symptoms over a 1-month period:
Delusions
Hallucinations
Disorganized speech
Disorganized behavior
Negative symptoms
(at least 1 of which must be a, b or c)
Individual’s premorbid level of functioning is affected in several major domains of life.
There must be continuous impairment over a period of at least 6 months, during which the individual might experience either active or residual symptoms.

runs.text: There must be continuous impairment over a period of at least 6 months, during which the individual might experience either active or residual symptoms.

blocks.text: These symptoms must not be due to the effects of substance usage or an underlying medical condition
Assessment
Assessment includes thorough history taking, physical examination, mental state examination and investigations
Non-Pharmacological Management

People with a first episode of psychosis are offered psychological interventions (family intervention and individual CBT) in conjunction with oral antipsychotics. CBT should be delivered on a one-to-one basis over at least 16 planned sessions
The re-evaluation of people's perceptions, beliefs or reasoning relates to the target symptoms
Also include at least one of the following components:
People monitoring their thoughts, feelings or behaviors with respect to their symptoms or recurrence of symptoms
Promoting alternative ways of coping with the target symptom
Reducing distress
Improving functioning.
Family intervention should:
Include the person with psychosis or schizophrenia if practical
be carried out for between 3 months and 1 year
Include at least 10 planned sessions
Take into account the whole family's preference for either single-family intervention or multi-family group intervention
Take into account the relationship between the main carer and the person with psychosis or schizophrenia
Have a specific supportive, educational or treatment function and include negotiated problem solving or crisis management work
Pharmacological Management
In acute attacks:
Treat like under section: Aggressive and Disruptive Behaviors in Adults.
For maintenance:
B: haloperidol (PO) 1.5-4.5mg 12hourly, increase by 1.5mg, every two weeks. Maximum dose 20 mg Daily
OR
A: chlorpromazine (PO) 100–400mg 24hourly in divided doses
OR
S: olanzapine (PO) 5–10mg titrate to maximum dose 20mg/24hours, given at night
OR
S: aripiprazole (PO) Start 10 -15mg OD, Maximum dose 30mg OD
OR
S: risperidone (PO) 1mg 12hourly then increase by 1mg every 2–3 days to 2–3mg 12 hourly. Maximum dose 6mg/day
OR
S: quetiapine (PO) Start 25mg, then increase by 25mg over one week to a Maximum dose of 300mg-400mg in divided doses a day

blocks.text: Caution:
Clozapine may cause:
Neutropenia (3% of cases) and agranulocytosis (0.8% of cases):
Pre-treatment: Baseline normal white cell counts and absolute neutrophil count.
Monitor absolute neutrophil count regularly.
Withdraw clozapine and review medication if neutrophils <1.0 x109/L (general population).
Myocarditis: highest risk in first two months of treatment. Monitor pulse, blood pressure, temperature; advise patient to report any palpitations, shortness of breath, chest pain, fever immediately.

Constipation: avoid anticholinergics; may require laxatives; prolonged discomfort may indicate intestinal obstruction.

Electroconvulsive Therapy (ECT)

ECT is an effective treatment for some types of severe mental illness. ECT uses an electric current to cause a seizure in the brain and is one of the fastest ways to treat severe symptoms of mental illness. ECT is done with the informed consent of the patient or following the patient's advance directives.

blocks.text: ECT is a safe and effective treatment with indications of its use in patients with schizophrenia including:
Treatment-resistant schizophrenia
To augment pharmacotherapy
Management of catatonia
Presence of Suicidal behavior
Severe agitation
Clozapine-resistant schizophrenia
ECT should be administered 2 to 3 times a week for a total of 6-12 sessions.
